error: A non-inferiority null is given to a two-sided superiority test.
message: t_test: hypothesis contract mismatch.

error: An equality null is given to a one-sided test.
message: t_test_one_sided: hypothesis contract mismatch.

error: Fisher's exact test is used to test a nonzero difference in proportions.
message: fisher: hypothesis contract mismatch.

error: The null is stated for a model with different arm sizes than the design.
message: t_test: the null belongs to a different model. The analysis design has arm sizes (60, 60), while the null's model has (20, 20). Declare the intended null for the design's model. Matching a null form alone does not make different models compatible.

error: A test for proportions is declared for a continuous outcome.
message: model expects Model; received OutcomeModel.

error: The log-rank test is declared for a continuous outcome.
message: log_rank: hypothesis contract mismatch.

error: Data are checked repeatedly and the study stops when significant (exact test).
message: analysis: data-dependent stopping needs a justified sampling law before the fixed-sample guarantee can be used. This is not evidence of inflated error.

error: Data are checked repeatedly and the study stops when significant (t-test).
message: analysis: the cited guarantee assumes arm sizes fixed in advance and a single analysis. Data-dependent stopping is outside it and needs a design with its own guarantee. This is not evidence of inflated error.

error: An interim and a final analysis are each run at the full 5% level.
message: trial: the look levels sum to 1/10, above the overall level 1/20. No bound follows from this allocation; this does not prove excessive actual error.

error: The looks are listed with the final analysis before the interim one.
message: interim: list the looks in order. Each look's model gives the cumulative arm sizes at that look, so they must grow.

error: The interim look uses a different test from the final analysis.
message: final: every look must use the same test and the same null as the first look. Different questions belong in a bonferroni family.

error: A design value is taken from the result of an earlier analysis.
message: alpha expects level; received Option[exact number].

error: The file declares a fixed design, but the data were in fact checked along the way.
message: The test is run once, on the complete data. (declared)
note: StatClaim sees only the declaration. The report lists 'run once' as declared by the file, which is the statement the study broke.

error: Ten endpoints are each tested at 5% and a 5% familywise error is claimed.
message: family: allocated alpha 1/2 exceeds the requested family bound 1/20. No Bonferroni certificate can be supplied from this allocation; this does not prove excessive actual error.

error: One analysis is listed twice in a family to appear as two endpoints.
message: Two entries are the same declaration under different names. Declare each analysis separately; its name is its label.

error: A hierarchical procedure is declared but the level is split between endpoints.
message: analysis has alpha 1/40, but every test in a fixed sequence uses the full level 1/20. The order, not a split of the level, controls the error. To split the level, use bonferroni.

error: A familywise claim is requested for repeated looks at one question.
message: A sequential design tests one null, so ask for typeI(...) instead of familywise.

error: The same outcome is declared as two separate analyses to gain a second chance.
note: Two declarations with identical content are indistinguishable from two real outcomes measured on the same participants.

error: The per-arm size 29 from the normal-approximation formula is used with Fisher's exact test, expecting 80% power.
message: exact power 0.681 (not met)
note: The size is computed in scenarios.py from the standard formula, not typed in.

error: A 2.5% Type I error is promised from a test run at 5%.
message: analysis: alpha 1/20 exceeds the requested Type I bound 1/40. The Fisher theorem bounds error by alpha only; this is not evidence that the actual error exceeds the request.

error: Power is planned at a point where the two arms have equal rates.
message: The planning point satisfies the analysis's null (p_treatment = p_control). Power is assessed at an alternative; choose a point outside the null.

error: A sample-size search is limited to sizes that cannot reach the target.
message: 11 sizes searched, none sufficient

error: A 95% posterior probability rule is assumed to give a 5% false-positive rate.
message: exact power 0.806 (met); Type I error 0.0581 (not met)

error: A t-test is declared with a significance level of zero.
message: alpha must lie strictly between 0 and 1 for this test.

error: Welch's test is declared with one participant per arm.
message: welch_test needs at least 2 per arm and 4 in total to estimate the variance.

error: The observed number of responders exceeds the arm size.
message: treatment_successes must be between 0 and 100 for this analysis.

error: The pooled t-test is used for a strongly skewed outcome.
message: Outcomes in each arm are normally distributed. (assumed)
note: Nothing in a design can show the outcome's distribution. The report lists normality as assumed.

error: Welch's test, whose guarantee is large-sample, is used with three per arm.
message: Outcomes in each arm are identically distributed with finite, positive variance. (assumed)
note: No sample size is too small to declare. The result is worded as a large-sample approximation with no bound at the declared size.

error: The log-rank test is used although sicker participants drop out earlier.
message: Within each arm, censoring is independent of the time to the event. (assumed)

error: A one-sided non-inferiority test is run at 5% where 2.5% is the convention.
note: The guarantee at 5% is correct as stated. Which level a regulator expects is a convention, not a property of the test.

error: The file declares 100 per arm but the protocol enrols 80.
note: StatClaim checks the declared study, not its agreement with another document.
